plan: This mechanism is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the clock exit price determines rank order, and the winner pays the second-highest bid, regardless of how the clock proceeds. In such auctions, bidding one's true value is a weakly dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. Since my value is $25, I should bid exactly $25 to ensure I win whenever profitable and never overpay relative to my valuation.

This auction functions like a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and my exit point is determined by my own bid. In such mechanisms, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy—it ensures I win whenever profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay, since I only pay the lower competing bid if I win. Bidding above or below my value only risks losses or missed profitable wins. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $18.

Since the payment rule is equivalent to a second-price auction (winner pays the second-highest sealed bid), bidding my true value is a dominant strategy. There's no benefit to shading up or down: bidding above value risks paying more than the prize is worth, and bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $31.
